s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular visual disturbance with optic disc swelling and retinal lesions in a young adult with a history of neurofibroma
salient_findings: Grey dot in central vision of left eye
Swollen optic disc in right eye
Parafoveal grey-white deep retinal lesion in left eye
Cotton-wool spot in posterior pole of left eye
Central scotoma in left eye
key_facts: 18-year-old Chinese woman
Known plexiform neurofibroma of the arm
No medical history, trauma, family history, smoking, coffee, tea, illicit drugs, or oral contraceptive use
Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg
Visual acuity 20/20 in right eye and 20/25 in left eye
No relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild subcapsular cataracts bilaterally
Bilateral vestibular schwannomas on brain MRI
Parasellar mass consistent with meningioma on brain MRI
Cervical extramedullary lesion on brain MRI
Normal carotid Doppler ultrasound and transthoracic echocardiography
Normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count and inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Neurofibromatosis type 1
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a known plexiform neurofibroma of the arm and bilateral vestibular schwannomas on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Paracentral acute middle maculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Swept-source optical coherence tomography of the left macula revealed hyperreflective bands in the inner nuclear layer consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with optic disc swelling and a small central scotoma in the left eye

shortlist.label: Neuroretinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of neurofibroma and presents with optic disc swelling and retinal lesions

shortlist.label: Papillophlebitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with optic disc swelling and a cotton-wool spot in the posterior pole, which are consistent with this condition

raw.rationale: The presence of a known plexiform neurofibroma, bilateral vestibular schwannomas, and a parasellar mass consistent with a meningioma are all characteristic findings of Neurofibromatosis type 1, which best explains the key facts without contradiction.

rejected.label: Paracentral acute middle maculopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has findings consistent with paracentral acute middle maculopathy, this condition does not account for the broader range of systemic and neurological findings.

rejected.label: Optic neuritis
rejected.why: The patient's visual acuity and lack of relative afferent pupillary defect do not support a diagnosis of optic neuritis as the primary explanation for her symptoms.

rejected.label: Neuroretinitis
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of inflammation or infection that would support a diagnosis of neuroretinitis.

rejected.label: Papillophlebitis
rejected.why: The patient's normal laboratory studies and lack of signs of inflammation make papillophlebitis an unlikely diagnosis.
